## Round 1 (gen1) findings: q09 specialisation
- Baseline q09 was about 918-980 ms. The old plan built hash tables on 15M orders and 8M partsupp. The LIKE contains filter got 0.2 selectivity.
- E0001 ACCEPTED: STRING_PATTERN_SELECTIVITY 0.05 in relation_statistics_helper.cpp ExtractGetStats. q09 went 980 to 723 ms.
- BuildProbeSideOptimizer (build_probe_side_optimizer.cpp TryFlipJoinChildren) compares row_width*cardinality, with penalties for VARCHAR/column count.
- SQL experiment trick: SET disabled_optimizers='join_order,build_side_probe_side' plus explicit JOINs (left=probe, right=build).

## Round 2: E0002 ACCEPTED (multi-key BF on first key), q09 723 to 536 ms (bench ~503 ms)
- CanUseBloomFilter (physical_hash_join.cpp ~761) now allows multi-key joins on condition 0. Join HT Finalize gathers key column 0 and hashes it for the BF.
- A BF is built only when it is pushed (SetBuildBloomFilter in PushBloomFilter), so no BF is built for nothing.

## Round 3: E0003 prefetch RETIRED at -4.7% (runs gave -5.7, -4.8, -9.9 with build prefetch, -5.6). Good idea, crude implementation, just under the bar.

## Round 4 KEY FINDING: profile operator times are badly inflated (about 4x on scans)
- Use wall time from batches: `dbe-tool sql "q; q; q"` prints the total for the batch; divide by N. The first query in a fresh process is cold (about 2-3x slower), so use 3+ copies.
- q09 is about 165 ms per run warm in a batch. Built up one piece at a time (count(*) versions):
  lineitem⋈part (BF) 20 ms | part⋈partsupp 12 ms | +2-key lineitem⋈partsupp probe about 30 ms | +orders join about 50-65 ms | the rest (supplier, nation, agg, projections) about 20 ms.
- So hash-join build/probe is about 90 of 165 ms, the main cost. The lineitem scan (3.6s in the profile) is only about 20-30 ms of wall time.
- The orders join HT holds 3.27M rows, so capacity 8M entries = 64MB (load factor 2, join_hashtable.hpp:408). 15M probes, about 80% misses. DRAM-bound.
- Bitpacking has NO select function (only RLE, constant, dict_fsst, fsst do). StandardColumnData::Select falls back to a full decode plus Slice. All lineitem columns are BitPacking. But measured: the extra 4 non-filter columns cost only about 13 ms of wall time at 5% selectivity, so a bitpacking Select is worth less than 10 ms on q09. Low priority (possibly useful for hidden selective scans).
- compressed_materialization helps q09 (disabling it: 128 vs 111 ms/run). Keep it.
- Orders BF retest: CM disabled, orders join mini-query 96 vs 82 ms with CM, so the orders BF is slower. Confirmed dead.

## Round 4 dispatch: prefetch v2 (build+probe always together, distance-based i+16, 4MB threshold, chain prefetch)
- If it is accepted: next, consider a branch-light first-probe in ProbeForPointersInternal (join_hashtable.cpp:188). The while(true) occupied/salt branches mispredict at about 41% occupancy.
- If it is retired again near -5%: prefetch is exhausted. Move on.

## Remaining ideas (ranked)
- Agg/projection tail about 20 ms: extract(year) plus the amount expression plus compress/decompress around HASH_GROUP_BY (175 groups). Small.
- 2-key join (30 ms): all probes hit, so row_matcher compares 2 columns column-at-a-time over 14MB of rows. Prefetch covers part of it.
- Multi-key join cardinality (backlog), low priority; the plan is already good.

## Tool notes
- `dbe-tool profile q09.m0 | grep -E "rows|[0-9]s|Table:|Conditions|="` gives a plan summary. `cut -c1-130` keeps it readable.
- `pragma_storage_info('tbl')` shows the compression per column segment.
- Bash rejects $VAR, for-loops with variables, and cat of relative paths. Inline the SQL text.

issues.title: Hash join prefetch v2: build insert + probe, software-pipelined, LLC-sized threshold
issues.hypothesis: Batch wall-clock timing (dbe-tool sql running 3-5 copies of a query; profile operator times are inflated about 4x by profiling) puts q09 at about 165 ms per run. Building it up one join at a time: lineitem⋈part (with BF) costs about 20 ms, partsupp⋈part about 12 ms, the 2-key lineitem⋈partsupp probe (3.27M probes, 1M-entry/8MB HT, 14MB of rows) about 30 ms, and the orders join (15M probes into a 3.27M-row build, so 8M entries = 64MB of ht_entry_t, with about 80% misses) about 50-65 ms. So about 90 of the 165 ms is hash-join build/probe, and that is bound by memory latency. The lineitem scan, although it shows 3.6s in the profile, is only about 20-30 ms of wall time. In ProbeForPointersInternal (join_hashtable.cpp:188) the salted linear-probe loop has a data-dependent `while(true)`/break on whether a slot is occupied (about 41% occupancy, so mispredictions are frequent). That stops the CPU from overlapping the DRAM misses. E0003 measured -5.7%/-4.8% with probe prefetch only, and -9.9%/-5.6% with build prefetch added, but the official run was -4.7%, just under the bar. This version differs as follows: (1) build and probe prefetch always ship together, since the build prefetch was the larger part of the gain; (2) prefetch runs a fixed distance ahead inside the loops (i+PREFETCH_DISTANCE, e.g. 16), not as a 2048-wide pre-pass, so it does not over-subscribe the line-fill buffers and gets no extra loop pass on small inputs; (3) it is gated on the HT entry array being larger than about 4MB (not 1MB), so mid-size HTs that fit in cache pay nothing; (4) it also prefetches the chained row in ScanStructure::AdvancePointers/Next when chains_longer_than_one is set.
issues.plan:
src/execution/join_hashtable.cpp only:
(a) Add a file-local helper `static inline void PrefetchRead(const void *p)` / `PrefetchWrite` that wraps __builtin_prefetch under #if defined(__GNUC__)||defined(__clang__), and is a no-op otherwise. Add a file-local constexpr PREFETCH_DISTANCE=16 and a constexpr byte threshold of 4MB, compared against ht.capacity*sizeof(ht_entry_t).
(b) ProbeForPointersInternal: when over the threshold, at the top of iteration i prefetch entries[hashes_dense[i+D] & ht.bitmask] if i+D<count. Use template dispatch, or a bool hoisted outside the loop, so the small-HT path is unchanged.
(c) GetRowPointersInternal: before row_matcher_build.Match, prefetch the row pointers for keys_to_compare_sel (pointers_result_v data) in a short loop. This touches only `keys_to_compare_count` pointers, which is cheap.
(d) InsertHashesLoop (the build): at the top of each insert iteration, prefetch the target entry for write at distance D.
(e) ScanStructure::AdvancePointers (or wherever the chain next pointer is followed) when ht.chains_longer_than_one: prefetch the next row pointer.
No header changes and no semantic changes.
issues.expected_gain: q09: 6-10% (E0003 already measured -5% to -10% with a cruder pass; the distance-based version plus the build prefetch should land at the upper end). Any query with a hash join whose HT exceeds the LLC should gain too.
issues.generality: Every hash join with a large build side (more than about 250K rows): star and snowflake fact⋈dim joins, fact⋈fact joins on orderkey, TPC-H Q3/5/7/8/9/18/21-style queries. Queries with small HTs skip it because of the threshold. Nothing can return different results, since prefetch is only a hint. Worst case is a few percent of extra instructions on large-HT joins that are already cache-resident (unlikely above 4MB).
issues.risk: Low for correctness. The risk is in measurement: the gain may again come in near the 5% noise bar. The implementer should bench q09 at least twice and report both runs.
